title: Relative serum chloride and albuminuria: a locked incremental-prediction test across two NHANES releases
abstract: Adding serum chloride/sodium ratio to a source-trained model containing separate sodium and chloride concentrations plus demographic, blood-pressure, glycemic, body-size and serum-creatinine measures yielded a weighted Brier gain of -0.00006345 in NHANES2009–2010 (n=5346;source NHANES2007–2008 n=4969). The source-and-target PSU-refit95% interval was [-0.00065974,+0.00039402]. Positive gain favors augmentation. The prespecified criterion of an interval wholly above zero was not met. This tests incremental representation for concurrent single-sample UACR≥30mg/g,not a new biomarker,causal effect,persistent albuminuria,or CKD diagnosis.
